text: This month, the rand slipped from about sixteen fifty to about seventeen fifty to the dollar.
asr: This month, the rand slipped from about 16.50 to about 17.50 to the dollar.

text: That one number travels through your whole budget.
Fuel first. Oil is priced in dollars, so a ninety dollar barrel now costs about ninety rand more.
asr: Fuel first. Oil is priced in dollars, so a $90 barrel now costs about R90 more.

text: Imports next. A phone priced at five hundred dollars costs about five hundred rand more.
asr: Imports next. A phone priced at $500 costs about R500 more.

text: Dearer fuel raises transport costs, and over time, food prices.
It all flows into inflation, already five point two percent.
asr: It all flows into inflation, already 5.2%.

text: And inflation is what the Reserve Bank watches when it sets interest rates.
The rand moves both ways. When it firms, these costs ease.
Mmzahnsee Money Matters. Know where your money is going.
asr: Mzansi Money Matters. Know where your money is going.
